clauses.text: Never PR a feature branch straight into `main`.
Keep this file current in the same PR.
A merge never cuts a tag. `/release` does.
Never push directly to `main`.
Never add `push` back to a release job's `if:`
Always delete a feature branch as soon as it's merged
A release is done only when the tag is read back from the re
clauses.rationale: The one rule. Every intermediate signal in this path can succeed while no tag is cut — a dispatch exits 0 for a run that later fails, a promotion can merge while the release job errors, and _release.yml no-ops on an existing tag so a 'successful' retry can correct nothing. Lose this line and the skill starts reporting releases that did not happen.

clauses.text: [Nn]ever ask about anything in that table
clauses.rationale: The whole preflight table is fact: the version on main, the last tag, the unreleased commit count, the blockers. Asking the user to confirm any of it is the UX failure that makes a skill feel like a form, and it is the reason this skill can get to a decision in two questions.

clauses.text: it never reimplements a single thing shipflow does
clauses.rationale: Every mutating step belongs to shipflow; this skill resolves the binary, gates its version, and shapes its output. The moment release.js grows its own version reading or PR opening, the two drift and a user gets different behaviour depending on which one they invoked — the exact failure shipflow's own SKILL.md warns about for CI scaffolding.

clauses.text: [Nn]ever run `cut` without naming the `collateral` list to the user first
clauses.rationale: A dev -> main promotion is a single merge of all of dev and cannot be made selective, so every other bumped-but-untagged component has its bump moved to main alongside the one being released. Until 2026-08-02 that also RELEASED them — the release jobs ran on push, so a merge tagged and npm-published everything within seconds, irreversibly. They are now workflow_dispatch-only and cut dispatches exactly one component, so the blast radius is gone; the disclosure stays because the user should still know what their promotion moves and which components are now one dispatch from a release nobody asked for.

clauses.text: API-stability promise, and no commit message is entitled to make it
clauses.rationale: Conventional-commit tooling maps a breaking change to a major bump, which for an 0.x component means silently declaring 1.0.0. shipflow caps it at minor and reports capped: true; this line is what makes the agent surface the cap rather than quietly accept it.

clauses.text: will usually return `done: false`, and that is not an error
clauses.rationale: cut is bounded and resumable because the full path outlasts a single call. Without this line an agent reads the first `done: false` as a failure and either reports the release as broken or starts working around it by hand with gh — abandoning every guard that makes the flow safe.

clauses.text: One script call, not a pipeline.
Report in tables, with named columns.
Never claim a visual result without the artifact.
Never print file contents into the conversation.
Announce the skill once, at the start
Keep the machinery invisible.
Show, don't describe.
It is raw material, not the entry.
`suggestedBumpCapped: true` must be said out loud.
Never run `cut` without naming the `collateral` list to the user first.
Never claim a result you did not observe.
Announce at start:
say which stage you reached and that the release did not happen.
Never ask about anything in that table.
